traits.description: A common condition influenced by many genes and strongly by weight, activity and diet. Single common variants shift odds modestly.

traits.description: Weight relative to height. Each common variant has a very small average effect.

interventions.summary: Most adults who have trouble digesting milk sugar can still handle about 12–15 g of lactose at a time (roughly a cup of milk), according to a review of randomized trials. Lactose-free products, probiotics and similar aids were not clearly shown to help.

outcomes.quote: Evidence was insufficient that lactose-reduced solution or milk with a lactose content of 0 to 2 g, compared with greater than 12 g, is effective in reducing symptoms of lactose intolerance.

limitations: Most included trials studied malabsorption rather than symptoms.
Genotype alone does not diagnose lactose intolerance.

Women with a history of VTE who are heterozygous for the factor V Leiden variant and women homozygous for the factor V Leiden variant with or without prior VTE should avoid estrogen-containing contraception and HRT.

limitations: Expert review (GeneReviews), not a trial.
Many people with the variant never develop a clot.

warnings.title: Consumer chips are unreliable for very rare variants
warnings.summary: In a study comparing SNP-chip calls with sequencing, most very rare variant calls from chips were wrong. Any rare pathogenic variant listed below must be confirmed with a clinical-grade test before it means anything.

quotes.quote: for variants that are very rare in the population, with a frequency below 0.001% in UK Biobank, the positive predictive value was very low and only 16% of 4757 heterozygous genotypes from the SNP chips were confirmed with sequencing data
20/21 individuals analysed had at least one false positive rare pathogenic variant that had been incorrectly genotyped
SNP chips are extremely unreliable for genotyping very rare pathogenic variants and should not be used to guide health decisions without validation.

warnings.title: BRCA1/BRCA2 results from consumer chips are usually wrong
warnings.summary: In the same study, most BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants reported by SNP chips were not confirmed by sequencing, and people with a chip-only positive result had cancer rates similar to controls.

quotes.quote: For pathogenic variants in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes, which are individually very rare, the overall performance metrics for the SNP chips versus sequencing in the UK Biobank were: sensitivity 34.6%, specificity 98.3%, positive predictive value 4.2%, and negative predictive value 99.9%.

notes.title: About 'epigenetic' diets
notes.text: Epigenetic marks (such as DNA methylation) sit on top of your DNA and change with age and cell type. Your AncestryDNA or 23andMe file reads DNA letters only; it measures no epigenetic marks at all. Nutrients that feed methylation (folate, B12, B6, riboflavin, choline) are sometimes sold as 'epigenetic' diets. A systematic review of human trials found limited evidence that diet changes methylation, apart from folic acid in the colon, and pooled human trials of folic acid found no significant change compared with placebo. The closest genotype-specific evidence in this area is MTHFR TT and riboflavin, which lowered blood pressure in trials (see MTHFR).

evidence.value: Methylation changes with age and cell type
evidence.quote: Patterns of DNA methylation change during development and ageing, differ between cell types, are altered in multiple diseases and can be modulated by dietary factors.
evidence.citation: ElGendy et al., Br J Nutr 2018

evidence.quote: In summary, there is limited evidence from intervention studies of effects of dietary factors, other than folic acid, on DNA methylation patterns in humans.
evidence.citation: ElGendy et al., Br J Nutr 2018

evidence.value: Folic acid: hypermethylation in colorectal mucosa
evidence.quote: Meta-analysis of the effect of folic acid on global DNA methylation revealed strong evidence that supplementation caused hypermethylation in colorectal mucosa

evidence.value: Human trials: no significant change vs placebo
evidence.quote: However, meta-analysis of human clinical trials showed that folic acid supplementation did not promote significant changes in DNA methylation when compared to placebo.

notes.title: Does DNA-based diet advice work better?
notes.text: In the largest trial of personalised nutrition (Food4Me, seven European countries), tailored advice improved diets more than generic advice, but adding genetic results did not make it work any better. A GRADE review of gene–diet studies for omega-3 found most of the evidence weak. That is why this guide says, for each gene, whether your genotype actually changes the advice.
